## Summary

- **gammart is validated against GATE** (1,508 columns of a 10^14^-primary GATE matrix, pull rms 1.008; same reconstructions within 1–4 %), at 1.35 GPU-min instead of ≈ 4.9 × 10^5^ core-hours
- **Paper-2 checks (2026-10-28):** spectrum mismatch explained and window counts agree to 0.999–1.004 (**final**); converging-pixel matrix ≈ 1 % on 5 modules (**prototype**); full-system GATE (WP3, 29 Oct): **checkpoint passed**, GATE/gammart 1.002–1.003
- **Reconstruction:** OSEM 8 subsets with attenuation correction in the model; the best images of every phantom are shown
- **PI's question:** the line's 3.5 mm is the 2 mm grid floor of an isolated hot line. For extended objects the system gives **≈ 5–6 mm** (6 mm rods separate, 5 mm partly). Explanation: sharp core on a broad base. **Provisional: the validation chain is planned, not run**
- **Apertures:** uniform size C beats the current mix (8 mm V/P 0.41 vs 0.48, ±0.02); mixes never win; placement is second-order. **Provisional** (one matrix for data and recon, parallel pixels)
- **Not available yet:** formula vs system matrix, measured impulse response, numbers for commercial systems

::: {.notes}
One-line version for the PI: the simulation chain is trustworthy where tested, the resolution story is coherent but not yet proven, and the aperture result says build uniform if the inventory allows.
Sources: docs/engine, paper2_plan.md (WP0/WP1/WP2, 2026-10-28), resolution_consistency_plan.md, design_surrogate/_variables.yml.
:::

## Decisions and asks for the PI

| # | decision | proposal |
|:-:|:--|:--|
| 1 | **Aperture choice** | Inventory not binding: **uniform, size C**. Binding: **annealed placement** (small, repeatable gain). Drop index-mod-4: it is an ordinary random map |
| 2 | **Resolution number in paper 2** | Derenzo (smallest separable rods, stated iterations, noise, filter) **plus** the system-only impulse response. Never "the NEMA 3.5 mm" |
| 3 | **Run the resolution chain** | Phase 0 done; approve Phases 1–2 (measured impulse response in the Derenzo, 6 perturbed reconstructions) |
| 4 | **Publication order** | **Engine paper → system + apertures paper → surrogate paper** (last, heavy review) |
| 5 | **Scope of paper 2** | Energy window by simulation, scatter-correction method, comparators (LEHR, AdaptiSPECT-C, G-SPECT-I), XCAT / mesh50 in or out |

::: {.notes}
Decision 1: placement is a permanent build-time choice (decided 2026-10-27). The 18/18/18/19 inventory is the constraint. Map-to-map variation of the 8 mm V/P is ±0.04, larger than the placement effects between types; annealed gains V/P 7 mm −0.035.
Decision 4: paper 2 cites paper 1 and never re-claims its validation; paper 3 needs paper 2's aperture result.
:::

## The system

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
![](img/helmet_schematic.png){width=100%}
:::
::: {.column width="38%" .side-notes}
- **73 pinhole modules** on a helmet around the head, stationary, every brain point seen by many modules
- Module: tungsten **knife-edge** pinhole + **CsI(Tl)**, **25 × 25 pixels** (625 bins; 73 × 625 = 45,625 bins in all)
- **Four pinhole sizes** (A < B < C < D, range 0.5–2.0 mm), assigned by head index: **index mod 4**
- Small pinhole: sharp but dim. Large: bright but blurred
- Paper-2 detector: pixels **converging on the pinhole** (no parallax), 11.8 % energy resolution at 140 keV, window 126–154 keV
- Schematic only: exact geometry is confidential (system going commercial)
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Source: paper2_plan.md sections 2-3; design_surrogate article. The projection of a point is inverted and scaled by f/b (pinhole-to-detector over object-to-pinhole distance).
:::

## From phantom to image: data and model

![](img/pipeline.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fig-notes}
- **Data:** GATE 10 Monte Carlo of a phantom in the helmet, 15 mCi, 15 min (OSPool, Expanse, ERIS); photons tagged, so we can reconstruct the unscattered main-window counts
- **Model:** the system response matrix (SRM). GATE SRM: 10^14^ primaries, ≈ 4.9 × 10^5^ core-h, 4.2 % noise per element. **gammart SRM:** ray tracing on RT cores, deterministic, no Monte Carlo noise, 1.35 min
- **Reconstruction:** OSEM 8 module subsets, attenuation in the model (ray-traced factors per phantom), Gaussian post-filter, 2 mm grid
:::

## Earlier update 2: rim streaks

- Radial streaks at the rim of the field of view are a **property of the system matrix**, triggered by sources in the poorly sampled rim zone: **not truncation**
- A uniform object streaks only when its activity reaches the support edge
- The bright ring inside hot edges is the **maximum-likelihood edge overshoot** (Snyder et al. 1987)
- Advice: reconstruct with a small start value (≈ 0.01) outside the body contour, not a uniform start over the whole sphere

::: {.notes}
Source: reports/2026-10_rim_streaks/src/report.md (Summary table; confidence high for the SRM origin, medium for the insert-driven part). The study used noise-free consistent data.
:::

## Earlier update 3: phantom reconstruction, 14 Oct

- With **support restriction, TEW scatter correction and attenuation correction** the activity is recovered quantitatively
- SRMs with **2, 1.5 and 1 mm voxels give the same contrast and resolution** at every iteration, even on data made with the 1 mm SRM
- Decision: keep the **2 mm SRM** (5.5× faster than 1 mm); spend effort on convergence instead
- Error budget set up (19 Oct): at the reference setting the post-filter is the budget

::: {.notes}
Source: reports/2026-10_phantom_recon/quarto/slides.qmd (Summary), error_budget.qmd.
:::

- **OSEM 8 = MLEM at equal updates, 8× faster**, provided AC is in the model

- Without a post-filter nothing settles; **OSEM 8, 8000 updates, 8 mm filter** is stable: a citable reference

## Analytical baseline: classic pinhole formulas

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
$$R = \sqrt{R_g^2 + R_i^2},\qquad R_g = \frac{d_e\,(b+f)}{f}$$

$$g_k = \frac{w^2\cos^3\theta}{4\pi r^2}\quad\text{(Anger sensitivity)}$$

- $d_e$: effective pinhole diameter, including **knife-edge penetration** (Paix 1967; Metzler 2001)
- $b$, $f$: object–pinhole and pinhole–detector distances
- Unit tests: sensitivity within 0.1–0.2 %, penetration within 0.5 % (on axis): **single pinhole, not the brain system**
- **Brain system: Phase 0 done** (gammart): sensitivity 0.98 of the formula, aperture width within 1 %; quadrature $R$ 15–30 % high at the centre
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
![](img/classic_resolution.png){width=100%}
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Sources: resolution_theory.py / resolution_theory.md (table, uniform plane); tests/test_multi_pinhole.py.
This is the resolution of ONE PROJECTION. Best single module 5.0-8.4 mm nominal (r = 65 to 0), 5.5-9.1 with penetration; count-weighted 10.4-14.4 / 11.0-15.2 mm. The reconstruction beats these because the matrix models the blur and views are combined.
Phase 0 done 28 Oct (gammart, 2e10 photons/design, 7 points): sensitivity 0.975-0.989 of the formula, aperture spot width within 1 %, f = 27.0-27.4 mm; the quadrature R is 15-30 % high at the centre and misses parallax off-centre (parallel pixels). Details: 2026-10-28_analytic_resolution.
:::

- **Images** (same GATE data, OSEM 8, AC): contrast, FWHM and ROI ratios within **1–4 %**; e.g. 12.7 mm sphere 0.593 / 0.593, rods 7.9 mm 0.596 / 0.585; NEMA line FWHM 3.50 / 3.51 mm

## Paper-2 check WP0: the spectrum mismatch is explained (final)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](img/wp0_spectra_t2.png){width=100%}
:::
::: {.column width="40%" .side-notes}
- Point source, full system: GATE had **1.6 % more singles**, all at 60–100 keV
- **Room-air backscatter** in GATE's default air world (gone in vacuum)
- **Doppler broadening** (option4, Livermore) smears scatter below the 90.4 keV single-scatter limit; gammart has no Doppler
- Standard physics in vacuum agrees with gammart (0.96 ± 0.05)
- **Photopeak window within 1 % for all four GATE variants**
- WP1 and WP3: vacuum world, option4 reference
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Source: paper2_plan.md, WP0 results (2026-10-28); out/wp0/bands_t2.json; figure out/wp0/spectra_t2.png. 3e8 GATE primaries vs 4e9 gammart photons.
:::

:::: {.columns}

![](img/wp1_checkpoint.png){width=100%}
:::

- **WP1 (final):** window counts GATE / gammart **0.9991–1.0035** in 10 cases (0–45°, off-axis, 2 aperture sizes), errors 0.05–0.5 %
- Fluorescence in GATE removes **1.7 %** (0°), 2.0 % (30°), 16 % (45°) of window counts: gammart does not model it yet
- Converging pixels remove parallax (spot FWHM 1.91 → 1.81 mm vs parallel 1.73 → 2.25 mm)
- Edge triangle: 0.12–0.16 % of window events for a central point source, but **6–7.5 % for the extended Jaszczak and triple-line phantoms** (WP3, worst module 22 %): an open modelling/design decision
- **WP2 (provisional, prototype):** matrix vs MC ≈ 1 % on 5 modules; **top module 3.5 % off, unexplained**; no phantoms, no full 73-module matrix yet
- **WP3 (29 Oct): checkpoint passed.** GATE / gammart in-window counts 1.002–1.003 (fluorescence off) in all three phantoms; K-escape costs 2.0 %; recon V/P within 0.003
:::
::::

## The PI's question: 3.5 mm on the line, 6 mm on the Derenzo

![](img/resolution_measures.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fig-notes}
- Same reconstruction (GATE data, 2 mm SRM, OSEM 8, AC). **Triple line:** NEMA 3.5 mm (constant 50–1000 it = grid floor); Gaussian fit 0.5–1.4 mm. **Derenzo:** equivalent Gaussian 4.3–7.0 mm, depending on rod size. **Spheres:** 5.3–10.4 mm. **Ideal response (noiseless matrix):** 6.7–10.9 mm, regularisation-dependent. **Projection formula:** 7.6–14.0 mm
:::

## Working explanation: a sharp core on a broad base

![](img/core_base_schematic.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fig-notes}
- **The line is alone:** its width reads the core (and OSEM sharpens isolated hot sources further). **The rods are neighbours:** each receives the base of its neighbours' response, so the valleys fill up. Illustration with invented widths
- **Provisional:** Phase 0 (formula → matrix) is done; matrix → impulse response → phantom (Phases 1–3) is not. The noiseless ideal response shows only a weak tail (1.5–3 % beyond 15 mm), so the core/base picture still needs the measured OSEM response
:::

## The system-only impulse response: the earlier number was Monte Carlo noise

![](img/ideal_lir_profile.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fig-notes}
- Ideal local impulse response (regularised minimum norm, α = 10^−3^ λ~max~), current mix, parallel pixels. **The earlier 6.7 / 6.1 / 5.2 mm came from the GATE matrix, whose entries are Monte Carlo counts of 1–6: the noise makes a narrow spike plus a far-field tail.** Noiseless gammart matrix: **10.9 mm** (r = 0), 9.3 (r = 60), 6.7 (r = 95); adding GATE-like counting noise to gammart reproduces the spike
- The width also depends on α, so it is **not an absolute resolution**: quote the phantoms (Derenzo 6 mm rods, sphere edges 5.3–6.7 mm), which match between gammart- and GATE-matrix reconstructions. Use the ideal response to compare designs: converging pixels −1 to −2 mm, uniform C ≤ current mix
:::

## Which number for which use

| use | number | status |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **System, extended activity** | **≈ 5–6 mm**: 6 mm rods separate (V/P 0.08; 0.22 with 4 mm filter), 5 mm partly (0.36; 0.62) | quote with iterations, noise, filter |
| System only (object independent) | no absolute number: ideal response 6.7–10.9 mm (noiseless, α-dependent); for design comparison only | withdrawn as a resolution |
| Cold spheres, edges | 5.3–6.7 mm (1600 it); 8–10 mm (200 it) | provisional |
| **Hot line (NEMA)** | **not a resolution**: 3.5 mm = grid floor; fit 0.5–1.4 mm = OSEM sharpening | final |
| One projection | best module 7.6–8.4 mm; count-weighted 12.5–14.0 mm (r = 48 mm) | checked by Phase 0 |

::: {.notes}
Source: resolution_consistency_plan.md; V/P values at 8000 updates from boot_stats.json (± 0.005–0.012).
:::

## The validation chain is planned, not done

| phase | what | status |
|:--|:--|:-:|
| 0 | brain-system SRM against the classic formulas (18 points + 6 Derenzo sectors, per module) | **not run** |
| 1 | measured local impulse response inside the Derenzo recon (15 points, 6 perturbed recons, 20–1000 it) | **not run** |
| 2 | predict Derenzo V/P and sphere profile by convolving the truth with the measured response (within 2 SD or 0.05) | **not run** |
| 3 | triple line on the 1 mm grid (should fall below 3.5 mm); impulse response at the line, air vs water | **not run** |

- **The explanation on the previous slides is provisional until these are done**
- Possible output: a section of paper 2, or a short standalone paper; not paper 1

Source: resolution_consistency_plan.md. Phase 1 compute: ERIS gpu-l40s array or the workstation overnight; impulses ≥ 60 mm apart share a reconstruction (4 batches) plus a cross-talk and a linearity check.
:::

## Neural surrogate: a fast stand-in for the exact physics

![](img/surrogate_concept.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fig-notes}
- **Exact:** ray tracing of one module costs ≈ 20 min per design. **Surrogate:** a network that has seen 196,608 exact answers returns the same in ≈ 2 s (≈ 600×), **with slopes**, so the computer can ask "which pinhole width or head move improves the image fastest?"
:::

## Why one module describes the whole system, and how accurate it is

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](img/training.png){width=100%}
![](img/accuracy.png){width=80%}
:::
::: {.column width="50%" .side-notes}
- **All modules are identical up to pose and width;** shield and neighbours change nothing (2 × 10^−8^): learn **one** module, any design is a set of lookups
- **Training:** exact gammart labels at 196,608 source positions and 48 widths (34 min), values **and** derivatives; 584,840 parameters, 1.8 h
- **Accuracy (held-out widths):** values **0.20 %**, derivatives **0.75 %**, module totals **0.14 %** (median); whole designs: objective to 4.8 × 10^−4^
- **Optimiser result** (proxy, sensitivity ≥ 0.95): resolution width −6.3 % (continuous widths); poses add nothing under patient clearance; −10.7 % if modules could move freely (not reachable)
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Source: design_surrogate/_variables.yml, _tables/accuracy.md, _tables/optimisation.md; article.qmd for the architecture. Analogy: a chess player who has seen 200,000 positions answers instantly what an engine needs minutes to calculate.
:::

| current mix | 0.87 | 0.48 | 0.776 | 0.448 |

## Why uniform wins: information adds, one band has one winner

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](img/info_adds.png){width=100%}

::: {.fig-notes style="font-size:0.62em"}
**Terms.**
**Spatial frequency**: 1 / period of a bar pattern (0.1 cycles/mm = 10 mm period: 5 mm hot, 5 mm cold).
**MTF** (modulation transfer function): fraction of a pattern's contrast one head passes at that frequency; 1 for coarse patterns, toward 0 for fine ones; a bigger pinhole falls off sooner.
**Sensitivity**: fraction of emitted photons the head detects.
**F, Fisher information**: how precisely the data pin down the pattern at that frequency (higher = less noise); $F_h$ = head $h$'s share.
**Multi-scale objective**: a task needing several detail sizes at once.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="42%" .side-notes}
- **Information adds across heads:** $F=\sum_h F_h$. At one frequency a head contributes about *sensitivity × MTF²*
- A big pinhole: many counts, blurred. A small one: sharp, few counts. **Every frequency band has one best size, the same for every head**
- A mix lies **between** the pure designs: it cannot beat the best pure design at any frequency
- Mixing could win only for **multi-scale** objectives or apertures with MTF zeros: not knife-edge pinholes
- **Continuous widths still gain slightly:** heads differ in distance and angle, so each has its own best size (per-head tuning)
- Illustration with invented widths
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Source: design_surrogate/why_uniform_wins.md. Caveats toward large or uniform: inverse crime; no design resolves ≤ 6 mm rods; fixed count regime. Cheap confirmation (not run): summed information spectrum of each design, and a multi-scale objective.
:::

## What limits the image now: the error budget

| step (rods 7.9 mm, 8000 updates, 8 mm filter) | contrast (truth 1.00) |
|:--|:-:|
| 2 mm voxel grid | 0.89 |
| + 8 mm post-filter | 0.32 |
| + noise-free reconstruction | 0.30 |
| + Poisson noise (GATE data) | 0.29 ± 0.01 |

- **At the reference setting the post-filter is the budget**; everything after costs ≤ 0.04
- Unfiltered: system + algorithm lose most (0.89 → 0.70); **counting noise dominates the image error** (NRMSE 0.25 noise-free vs 1.26 with noise)
- Small: discretisation, attenuation inside a voxel, noise bias (≤ 0.03); model mismatch χ²/pixel 1.18
- Not in these numbers: object scatter, real detector response; gammart omits fluorescence (≈ 2 % of window counts) and Doppler

::: {.notes}
Source: 2026-10_phantom_recon/quarto/error_budget.qmd, read through eb_data.py (a('rods_7.9mm') 0.89, a(...,8) 0.32, s('B',...) 0.30, s('E') 0.29 ± 0.01; s('C','nrmse_phantom') 0.25, s('D') 1.26; CHI2 1.18).
:::

## Backup: classic formulas, values and validation

| level | analytic reference | status |
|:--|:--|:--|
| single pinhole, sensitivity | disc solid angle on axis; Anger $d^2\cos^3\theta/(16h^2)$ off axis | unit test < 0.1–0.2 %; not the brain system |
| single pinhole, penetration | knife-edge sensitivity-effective diameter (Paix; Metzler) | unit test < 0.5 %, on axis only |
| brain system, projection resolution and sensitivity | $R=\sqrt{R_g^2+R_i^2}$, $g_k = w^2\cos^3\theta/(4\pi r^2)$ | computed, **never compared with the SRM** |
| reconstructed resolution | linearised MLEM impulse response (Barrett, Wilson, Tsui 1994); penalised: $(F+\beta R)^{-1}F e_j$ (Fessler, Rogers 1996) | theory in `fisher_svd_gram.typ`; ideal response computed; no FWHM, no comparison with measured response |

- Uniform plane, best single module 5.0–8.4 mm (nominal) / 5.5–9.1 mm (penetration) from r = 65 to 0 mm; count-weighted 10.4–14.4 / 11.0–15.2 mm
